## PCR Primer Design

**Core parameters**

- Length: 18–22 bp is the sweet spot. Shorter risks mispriming, longer rarely helps.
- Tm: 58–65°C per primer, within 3°C of each other. Use the nearest-neighbor method (SantaLucia 1998), not the Wallace rule — Wallace is only reliable below ~15 bp.
- GC content: 40–60%. Aim for ~50%.
- GC clamp: end the 3' end with 1–2 G/C bases, but no more than 3 consecutive G/C in the last 5 bases.
- Avoid: runs of ≥4 identical bases, repetitive sequence, 3'-end complementarity between the two primers.

**What actually trips people up**

- Self-dimers and hetero-dimers are the most common silent killer. Run both primers through IDT OligoAnalyzer before ordering — check hairpin ΔG and dimer ΔG. Anything worse than −9 kcal/mol at the 3' end warrants redesign.
- Always BLAST your primers against the full genome, not just the transcript. Pseudogenes and paralogs catch you off guard.
- For high-GC templates (>65%), adding 5% DMSO or 1 M betaine to the reaction rescues more amplifications than redesigning the primers.
- If you're adding restriction sites or attB/attL sequences to the 5' end for cloning, only the 3' binding region needs to follow the Tm and GC rules. Add 4–6 random bases before the restriction site to allow efficient enzyme cutting.
- Amplicon size: 100–500 bp for genotyping; 80–150 bp for qPCR; 300–800 bp for Sanger sequencing of the product.

---

## CRISPR-Cas9 Knock-in Protocol

This covers RNP delivery by electroporation with an ssODN HDR template, which gives the best HDR:NHEJ ratio in most dividing cell lines.

**sgRNA design**

- 20 nt spacer + NGG PAM (SpCas9 standard)
- Target within 30–50 bp of the intended insertion site — HDR efficiency drops off sharply with distance
- Avoid runs of ≥4 Ts in the spacer (premature termination if using U6-driven transcription)
- Rank guides by on-target score (Rule Set 2 / Azimuth) and check for off-targets with Cas-OFFinder or CRISPOR

**ssODN template design**

- Homology arms: 60–90 nt on each side. Longer arms help for insertions >40 bp; shorter arms (40 nt) work fine for single-nucleotide edits.
- Mutate the PAM or seed region (positions 1–12 from PAM) in the ssODN to prevent re-cutting after HDR. 2–3 silent point mutations are enough.
- Use the strand complementary to the sgRNA spacer (i.e., the non-template strand) — meta-analyses lean slightly toward this, though the effect is cell-type dependent.

**RNP complex formation**

| Component | Amount per 2×10⁵ cells |
|---|---|
| SpCas9 protein (∼160 kDa) | 5 μg (~31 pmol) |
| sgRNA (synthetic, 2-piece crRNA+tracrRNA or single-guide) | 2–3 μg (~62–90 pmol) |
| Cas9:sgRNA molar ratio | 1:2 (Cas9:sgRNA) |
| ssODN | 2–5 μg |

RNP assembly: mix Cas9 + sgRNA in PBS or buffer, incubate 10 min at RT. Add ssODN to the cell suspension just before electroporation, not to the RNP mix — it doesn't need to complex with Cas9.

**Electroporation conditions (starting point for HEK293T)**

- Neon: 1150 V, 30 ms, 2 pulses
- Lonza SE solution, program CM-130 for HEK293
- Scale: 2×10⁵–1×10⁶ cells per reaction

Optimize pulse voltage first (±50 V steps), then pulse count. Viability and editing efficiency trade off — a 70–80% viability after electroporation is a reasonable target.

**HDR enhancers (optional but meaningful)**

- M3814 (DNA-PKcs inhibitor): 1 μM, add for 24–48 h post-electroporation — typically 2–4× improvement in HDR rate
- RS-1 (RAD51 stimulator): 7.5 μM, less consistent than M3814 but additive in some lines
- Cell cycle sync at G2/S with thymidine double block before electroporation helps if you need to maximize HDR and your cell line tolerates it

**Screening**

- Run a T7E1 or TIDE assay on a pool 48–72 h post-transfection to confirm Cas9 is cutting before spending time on clonal screening
- For knock-in confirmation, design one PCR primer inside the insert and one outside the homology arm — this avoids false positives from residual ssODN carryover
